card: A volcano forms where magma, which is hot melted rock, rises through the Earth's crust. Many volcanoes form at plate boundaries.

a.q: Why do some people choose to farm on land near a volcano?
opts: Volcanic soils are rich in minerals
Volcanoes never erupt near farms
Lava turns into water for crops
Plate boundaries stop eruptions
a.why: Over many years, ash and lava break down into soil rich in minerals, so crops can grow well. The option about eruptions never reaching farms is wrong, because the card says ash can cover farms and towns.

b.q: Mt Kelara, a volcano, last erupted 300 years ago. Today, farms cover its lower slopes. Which statement best explains this?

Gas from eruptions warms the soil so crops grow
b.why: Over many years, ash and lava from past eruptions break down into soil rich in minerals, which suits farming. The option about fresh ash is wrong, because fresh ash can harm crops: the benefit comes only after it breaks down over time.
b.clue: Think about how long it takes ash and lava to become soil.
